title: Folly of Idolatry
english: The devil makes thieves and preaches a false hope of holy things to those who do not have it, leading them astray from the path of righteousness, and he also preaches the tripartite hope of holy things.

If he is driven by fleshly movements, like gusts of wind, and is carried backward, then all our security walks towards nothing, with sin being strengthened in us by our will; we will be like sheared sheep, giving our purity to unclean demons, and like an untended vineyard, we are easy prey for those who plunder; and we will be overcome by unprofitable desires, and our strength will be spent in vain.

But if each person desires not to experience such things, let them accept fasting, the mother of all dignity, and subjugate the body, and through willing to suffer, let them fence their property with thorns, as one of the wise among us said; for the more perfect, it is enough to taste teachings, and they will be able to do so easily; but for those who need to go out to hunt, let them gather from everywhere what seems useful to them, and let them gather all things from everywhere that appear to be profitable to them.

However, I think they will not need much labor, for enthusiasm will carry them to being able to accomplish, like a river's current, constantly wearing away the opposing banks and making the opposing currents disappear, and also rendering the opposing desires invisible with unprofitable desires.

And what is greatest, it is necessary to add the remaining part of the danger, for God helps those who are struggling, and He will be with them to the end; and the power and strength of all things become a source of support and guidance, like a staff and sinews that provide stability and direction, and the power of all things.
The wisest of men, Melodius, will testify to this, saying that the staff and the voice of God have called him to a life of peace and devotion.

As we look around us, we see that the fruits of peace towards God are indeed bright and worthy of admiration, and that those who are rooted in the Church are like newly sprouted seeds that are hastened to growth by the experiences of the farmers and the supplies of water, and examining the natures of things as much as possible.

The prophet's voice echoes in our minds, urging us to make peace for those who come, and to walk through faith from ignorance to education, and from lack of counsel to joyful thought, and previously to a life of error (Isaiah 52:7).

But where do those who come arrive from, or where are they going to rest, is a question that is worthy to be seen, and one that requires careful consideration and reflection, and this is what it means to live a virtuous and noble life, as is fitting for humans who are rational and made in the image of the Creator, and before.

However, there are those who have been deceived by the devil's cunning and have turned to idolatrous practices, saying to wood and stone 'You are my God' and 'You gave me birth' (Isaiah 44:17, 17:7-8), and they call this their vote, judging what is right, and they call it upon themselves.

They are full of foolishness and consider this to be their vote, judging what is right; they seem to preserve human nature in body, but in mind and spirit, and as much as they have in mind and its contents, they are no better than irrational animals.

Someone might think they have power even in this, if they were careful with their own affairs; but as the God and Master of all says through one of the prophets, 'See that their heart is hardened and they are deceived' (Isaiah 6:9-10); they are indeed deceived, having abandoned the straight path of knowledge of God.

Some individuals are led astray by foolishness and deceitful reasoning, which carries them away into every kind of imprudence, and they end up worshiping wood and stones, and considering the nature created through them to be greater than human nature.
They even ascribe dominion to things that they themselves are masters of, and this is a clear example of how far they have strayed from the truth.

On the other hand, there are those who abandon such a lowly worship and think they must flee to higher and more prominent creations, and they examine the positions of the stars and the paths of the sun and moon, introducing fire, water, air, and earth as the principles of things, and they mythologize about the conjunction of the elements as the root of created things.

However, they should seek the ruler and leader of the things mentioned, and ascend from the beauty of creations to the God who gives them beauty, and how, he said to me, did they destroy more greatly, or how did someone examine the nature of existing things more thoughtlessly?

If someone were to see a house or a ship that is skillfully constructed, they would not simply marvel at it in a worthless way, but rather, they would praise the construction and beauty of what they see, and immediately imagine the architect who created such a thing, because it is obvious to all that the creator of something beautiful and well-constructed is a being of great intelligence and skill.

However, there are those who are concerned only with the turns of words and varied studies, and they stop their thought at only what is visible, ignoring the journey beyond the mind, and as a result, they do not see the God who is the creator and craftsman of all things, and they do not give him the glory that is due to him as the Lord and maker of all things.

If they were to exert all their effort to run to the utmost foolishness concerning the Father, it is unlikely that what they irrationally desire would be fulfilled, and the voice of the saint, as expressed by Paul, is true: 'The wisdom of this world is foolishness before God' (1 Corinthians 3:19).

We learn that the voice of the saint is true through the examination of events, and the Greeks introduce a multitude of gods into their lives, bringing in something unknown to those around them, and this unknown element is derived from a mixture of human and animal forms, resulting in an adulterated nature that is then presented as the norm.

By doing so, they corrupt the most beautiful image of humanity on earth, and it is pointless to dwell on the absurdity of such beliefs, so let us proceed to what is truly important, and a deep-seated ignorance pervades the minds of the Greek people, casting a gloom over their understanding and preventing them from seeking what is truly beneficial.

Instead, they settle for untested and false notions of truth and doctrine, and the foolish among them deprive humans of the best things in life, and their actions are a testament to the corrupting influence of such ignorance.

title: Free Will
english: Those who fulfill the debt of nature, which is their natural obligation, destroy their own autonomy, because they do not believe they have control over their own choices, nor do they wish to be masters of their own will.

Instead, they attribute the blame for their actions to the votes of others, rather than taking responsibility themselves, and they claim that fate and birth balance the life of each individual, assigning the best things to some and opposing others.

This idea is similar to setting up a charioteer, only to entrust the charioteering to another, which means the charioteer would not be responsible for winning or losing, nor would they be accountable for any suffering that may occur.
The true responsibility lies with those who have control over the chariot, not with the one standing on it, and ultimately, the choice of the doer is what matters, and it is not attributed to others.

To further expose the foolishness of these people, we will examine their deeds and the myths that have been passed down among them, and by doing so, we will gather evidence to demonstrate that their doctrine is not rooted in ignorance, but rather in a lack of self-control and a failure to use their own judgment in their actions.

The stories of Tantalus, Tityus, and Ixion, as well as the troubles of Sisyphus, are often cited as examples of people who have been justly punished for their wrongdoing, with Tantalus being punished for his uncontrolled tongue and his shameful disease, Tityus being stretched out over nine acres and having his liver torn at by vultures as a proof of his uncontrolled lust, Ixion being punished with wheels and circular motions, and Sisyphus being forced to toil for a long time.

These punishments are seen as just and fitting for the crimes that these individuals have committed, but according to their own understanding, humans are subject to the necessities of fate, rather than being responsible for the things they have done wrong, and if the law of the just is known to us, that not the sinners, but others, are punished in their place, it will not be clear that nothing could be more wretched than the gods they have established, if those who have been entrusted to judge and distribute all things do not have the power to judge correctly.

For if it is known that the law of the just is such that not the sinners, but others, are punished in their place, it will be clear that nothing could be more wretched than the gods they have established, and it will be obvious to everyone that this is the case.
A man's foolishness corrupts his way, and he blames God in his heart (Proverbs 19:3).

If someone were truly free from foolishness, they would not have a corrupted path, nor would they blame God's nature, for those who have established their own mind as a guide and teacher, and as a noble judge, always strive to do the best, and they exchange the best counsel and action with a certain tone.

Human beings have the capacity to choose their own path in life, and they walk voluntarily in both directions, towards good or evil, and it is not fate or birth that determines a person's actions, but rather their own free will.

The evil demon, who is the father of sin, has deceived humanity and led them astray from God's command through deception, and he has dominated us and feared the free nature that is inherent in humanity, trying to convince us that we are not capable of doing better, that God has not given us the power to be sober-minded, and that a necessary yoke has been laid upon us, saying 'You yourselves are not responsible for not being able to do better; God has not placed sobriety in your power; a necessary yoke has been laid upon you; fate and birth control and it is necessary to do what seems to them'.

But this is a deception designed to lead us away from the truth and into the depths of sin, and the evil demon handles man with such deceptions, having stolen him away from the doctrines of truth, and makes him more prepared for every sin, for fate, placing the escape in the things according to himself, and saying that he is subject to the unbreakable bonds of birth, will not submit to any punishment for which he may seem to be guilty.

Let us heed the words of the heralds of the Church, who have put on Christ and bear the mind of truth, and let us strive for peace, and end the enmity that divides us, and let war and battle cease, and instead offer our right hands to the Savior, and through faith, we can ask for peace and say with the prophet, 'Lord, our God, give us peace; Lord, possess us, we know no other besides you, we call upon your name' (Isaiah 26:12-13).

This message will be beneficial for the Greek children and those who have recently entered the Church, and for those who are armed with the weapons of ignorance, trained as unwise soldiers, and are fighting against the truth.

title: Spiritual Circumcision
english: The one who submits to the Savior must do so through the shadow, type, and letter, having the form of knowledge in the law, as it is written, and must fight with the truth of deeds. Let us also help those who love each other and make peace with him. But until when, Jew, will you be devoted to the types from the letter and pass by the power of truth? When will the end of your ignorance be seen, and when will you turn your mind away from the shadow in the law? You think that God greatly rejoices over you when He sees you sacrificing oxen and being concerned with foods and their differences, and you have a lengthy and precise discussion about these things to boast about, and you even sacrifice animals with pleasure. These things are the exercises of the highest virtue, and you set for yourself the boundaries of approval in these things. However, I say that the wisdom and understanding of the lawgiver are greater than all speech and wonder.

You have left spiritual worship and have made the worse journey, being thickened by the density of the letter. Then you think to honor God through this, but you have rejected the most accurate grasp of the law, as if you have all knowledge of the written things, and you are not aware of being foolish. Come, let us discuss a few things with you, for you will understand very easily from here, if you have the will to be sober, that you spend long times in error. You receive circumcision in the flesh as a great thing and the most timely for worship. I would examine, and quite reasonably, the Jewish foolishness, for they do not understand readily and flee from learning, sinning in another way, and are led by their own ignorance to not enjoy any good things. But let them also listen to the prophetic voice, which says, 'Awaken, you drunkards, from your wine' (Isaiah 29:9 or 1:5). Let us consider what is useful from circumcision, or what benefit the lawgiver will bring to us through it. If the circumcision of the body parts, through which nature is served for generation, is imposed for a reason, unless it has a most beautiful reason, it would be ridiculous. Rather, it is written as the art of the creator, as if the body's shape is weighed down by certain superfluous things, like some excesses, which burden the body's form.

Then how, if the power of the things said is thus understood by us, do we not err in judging the divine mind to be faulty? For if in being circumcised the more saving things of the body's nature are preserved, how was this not better and more excellent from the beginning? Who, telling that the blameless and unblemished nature was born in faults of what is fitting, does not seem to be talking nonsense? For the God over all created irrational living beings. But nothing in the construction of these appears to be lacking or excessive towards the most precise beauty. God has completely avoided the accusation against both, and escapes the censure in each. How did God, being so wise, who made such great providence in lesser things, err in something most valuable? And did he prepare the one made in his image to appear more shameful among irrational beings, if nothing is lacking in those, but something is lacking in this one? The law given through Moses commands that a child be circumcised on the eighth day and brought to the Lord God, with the sacrifice of the custom previously performed on it. As it is written, our mind is the most fertile of all by nature, having in itself the seeds of all virtue and the desires for each of the beautiful things, always being provided with its own movements, as from the earth. For it has been made this way by the creator. But forgetfulness, like a kind of rust, spreads over it, which is the nourishment of all impurity. It either extends or is cast down like a cloud over the better things. The memory that overshadows the need to do the best things treats the earthly as a business instead of the spiritual, thus showing the person to be full of all impurity. To those to whom this has happened, it is said through a prophetic voice: 'Remember, you who are far from the Lord, and let Jerusalem come up into your heart' (Isaiah 49:14). For it was necessary, just like pouring water on fire, to pour the remembrance of good things on the evils that come from forgetfulness, and to abolish the remaining ones through opposing helps.

As we remain under the influence of forgetfulness, our minds are shrouded in darkness, and our natural inclination to produce good things is stifled by ignorance. We are unclean and detestable, and it is only by God's reckoning that we are considered worthy. However, when we reject the forgetfulness that has taken hold of us and cut away the errors that have arisen from it, we will be free from all wickedness and evil, and our minds will be fertile and productive. Through this process of transformation, we will be reborn into a state of innocence and simplicity, and we will stand confidently before God. We will not bring ourselves before him, just as a newborn child does not bring itself to God. Rather, it is Christ who will bring us, offering himself as a sacrifice to the Father, on the eighth day, which is after the lawful Sabbath, because this is the time of the coming of our Savior. For when we are in Christ, we become a new creation, and the old things pass away, giving way to a new reality (2 Corinthians 5:17). This concept is illustrated by the type of circumcision according to the flesh, which is completed on the eighth day and presents the newborn to God. The apostle Paul, with his profound wisdom, also bears witness to this truth, proclaiming that true Jewishness is not about outward appearances, but about the inner, spiritual reality, saying: 'For not the one in the visible is a Jew, nor is the circumcision in the flesh, but the one in the hidden is a Jew, and circumcision of the heart, not in letter, whose praise is not from humans, but from God' (Romans 2:29). And again he writes: 'Look at the dogs, look at the evil workers, look at the mutilation. For we are the circumcision, the ones serving God in spirit, and boasting in Christ Jesus, and not trusting in flesh' (Philippians 3:2-3). The value of physical circumcision is limited, and it is only when it is seen as a symbol of spiritual purification that it takes on true significance. By embracing this spiritual perspective, we can form a deeper understanding of our faith and avoid the suffering that comes from a superficial approach. This is in line with the prophetic word, which advises us to make a new beginning, saying: 'Make for yourselves new homes…'
